title: Identifying Conditional Policy Kernels in Latent Max-Linear DAGs from Spectral Laws
banked_reason: The theorem is sound and maximized within scope, but the projected paper-score ceiling is 6.6 below the 7.4 field threshold; no bounded in-scope repair closes the contribution gap.
gap_reasons: The result is a semantic CAD algorithm with no complexity guarantee or implemented decision, limiting its practical value.
The only worked witness has empty conditioning set and uses known edge redundancy, so it does not demonstrate the new conditional machinery on a singular stratum.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a terminating sound-and-complete CAD/QE decision theorem over the full positive-real edge-weight fiber, including exact one-sided overlap, singular faces, ties, coincident rays, and algebraic negative witnesses; both mathematical and rubric reviews passed without findings. The field-tier package failed on contribution significance rather than correctness: it supplies neither an implementation nor a useful complexity guarantee, and its sole worked witness does not exercise the new conditional singular-stratum machinery. A bounded same-topic repair could not close the resulting field-score gap, so the sound result was banked at subfield tier.
tldr: An exact algebraic observed spectral law determines the full positive-real compatibility fiber of a finite latent max-linear DAG. A terminating semantic algorithm checks whether the observed conditioning law is dominated by every compatible policy conditioning law, then returns a jointly Borel observed-law policy kernel valid for every real compatible model or two algebraic models whose conditional kernels differ on a positive-mass stratum. Singular faces, path ties, coincident rays, and conditioning-invisible shocks are retained; no completeness claim is made for a graphical calculus.
gap: Existing fixed-matrix conditional formulas and intervention rules do not compare conditional policy kernels across the whole algebraic spectral fiber. A closed support test misses positive-mass lower-dimensional faces.
fill: Prove canonical parameterized sign-cell and density calculus, semialgebraic conditional-kernel equality, and a total four-outcome decision with a finite grammar and terminating verifier for both positive and negative certificates.
